_page.title: Guide for Roblox Studio
_page.intro: From the downloaded ZIP to an accessory on your character: import, texture, accessory and a short script, step by step with screenshots.
zip.title: What's in the ZIP
zip.0.p: Every download is one folder named after the model. Inside you get:
zip.1.td.0.1: The model for Roblox Studio. Up to 4,000 triangles. Most models are already sized in studs; see Troubleshooting if yours is not.
zip.1.td.1.1: The color texture for the FBX model (1024 × 1024 px).
zip.1.td.2.1: A more detailed version for other 3D tools. It is not made for Roblox limits.
zip.1.td.3.1: What you may do with the model, with your license key.
zip.1.td.4.1: A short summary and a link to this guide.
zip.2.p: For Roblox Studio you only need the `.fbx` and the `_tex.png` file.
before.title: Before you start
before.0.steps.0: Install Roblox Studio and sign in. Buttons may move a little in newer versions than the one named above.
before.0.steps.1: Open a place to work in. A new **Baseplate** place is enough.
before.0.steps.2: Unzip the download. The ZIP opens into a folder with the model name, and the files are in another folder with the same name inside it.
before.1.p: Importing uploads the model and the texture to the Roblox account you are signed in with (**Upload to Roblox** is on by default). Use an account you are happy to upload to.
import.title: Import the model
import.0.steps.0: On the **Home** tab, click **Import**. Do not use the **Import** button inside the Terrain Editor; that one is for height maps.
import.0.steps.0.alt: Import button on the Home tab
import.0.steps.1: In the file dialog, pick the `.fbx` file from the ZIP.
import.0.steps.2: The **Import Preview** window opens. The default settings are fine. Before you click **Import**, fix the texture as shown in the next section.
import.0.steps.2.alt: Import Preview window with default settings
import.1.p: After the import, the **Import Queue** panel shows a green check, and a new `Model` with a `MeshPart` called `Handle` appears in `Workspace`. The model stands upright and faces the front.
texture.title: Apply the texture
texture.0.p: Most models show a `base_color_texture` row in **Import Preview** with a red mark: “Could not read the color map texture file associated with this object.” You can fix it right there.
texture.1.steps.0: In the tree on the left, click `base_color_texture` (under `world` ⟩ `Handle`).
texture.1.steps.1: Next to **Color File Path**, click the folder icon.
texture.1.steps.1.alt: Texture row with the error and the folder icon next to Color File Path
texture.1.steps.2: Pick the `_tex.png` file from the ZIP. The row gets a check mark. Click **Import**.
texture.1.steps.2.alt: Texture row checked after picking the PNG file
texture.2.p: Some models have no `base_color_texture` row at all and come in white. Add the texture after the import:
texture.3.steps.0: On the **Home** tab, click **Assets** to open the **Asset Manager**.
texture.3.steps.1: Click **Import** in the Asset Manager and pick the `_tex.png` file. In the **Import Queue**, click **Start Import**.
texture.3.steps.2: When the green check appears, find the image in the Asset Manager and note its number in the **ID** column.
texture.3.steps.2.alt: Asset Manager with the image ID
texture.3.steps.3: In **Explorer**, select the `Handle` part of the model. In **Properties**, type `texture` in the filter.
texture.3.steps.4: Click **TextureContent**, type `rbxassetid://` followed by the ID (for example `rbxassetid://1234567890`) and press Enter.
accessory.title: Turn it into an accessory
accessory.0.steps.0: On the **Avatar** tab, click **Accessory**. The **Accessory Fitting Tool** panel opens.
accessory.0.steps.0.alt: Accessory button on the Avatar tab
accessory.0.steps.1: Click the **Part** field, then click the model in the viewport. The field shows `Handle`. Click **Continue**.
accessory.0.steps.1.alt: Handle selected in the Accessory Fitting Tool
accessory.0.steps.2: Choose **Accessory**, then the accessory type from the table below. Leave **Select Body Type** as it is. A mannequin appears and the model moves to its place on it. Click **Continue**.
accessory.0.steps.2.alt: Accessory type Back chosen, the model sits on the mannequin
accessory.0.steps.3: The blue box shows the space the accessory may take. Click **Generate MeshPart Accessory** at the bottom of the panel.
accessory.0.steps.4: A small window says the accessory was generated into Workspace. It may open behind the main Studio window. Click **OK**.
accessory.1.p: The new `Accessory` is in `Workspace` and is named `Handle`, after the part. Rename it (for example `KabutoHelmet`) and delete the original imported `Model`, which has almost the same name, so you do not mix them up.
try.title: Try it on a character
try.0.steps.0: On the **Avatar** tab, click **Character**. In **Generate Rig**, keep **R15** and click **Block Avatar (2012)**. A figure called `Rig` appears in `Workspace`.
try.0.steps.1: In **Explorer**, drag your accessory onto `Rig`. It snaps to its place without any moving by hand.
try.1.alt: Backpack on the back of the test figure
game.title: Use it in your experience
game.0.steps.0: Move the accessory to `ServerStorage` and give it a name without spaces, for example `KabutoHelmet`.
game.0.steps.1: In `ServerScriptService`, add a `Script` with the code below. Change the name in `WaitForChild` to yours.
game.0.steps.2: Click **Play**. Your character wears the accessory.
troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.0.td.0.0: The model is white or grey.
troubleshooting.0.td.0.1: The texture was not applied. See [Apply the texture](#texture).
troubleshooting.0.td.1.0: The model is much bigger than the character.
troubleshooting.0.td.1.1: Select the imported `Model` in **Explorer**, type `scale` in the **Properties** filter and set **Scale** to a smaller number (for example `0.3`). Do this before the Accessory Fitting Tool.
troubleshooting.0.td.2.1: You used the Terrain Editor. Close it and use **Home** ⟩ **Import**.
troubleshooting.0.td.3.0: The fitting tool does not pick the model.
troubleshooting.0.td.3.1: Click the **Part** field first, then the model in the viewport.
troubleshooting.0.td.4.0: The “generated” window does not show up.
troubleshooting.0.td.4.1: It is behind the main Studio window. Move the main window or switch to it with the keyboard.
troubleshooting.1.p: If a model cannot be used at all, see [licenses and refunds](https://market.ol1n.com/licenses).
publishing.title: Publishing
publishing.0.p: Selling or sharing an accessory on the Marketplace has its own rules, checks and fees, set by Roblox. Read [Publish to Marketplace](https://create.roblox.com/docs/marketplace/publishing-to-marketplace) in the Roblox documentation before you try. Check also what your license allows.
